title: Coding-session sentiment meter: thanks vs. F-bombs
description:
Scan Ryan's local AI coding sessions and show a meter that balances how often he says thanks against how many F-bombs he drops — an indicator of how a day of vibe coding is going. Everything stays local; output is counts only.

Sources (v1 adapters): Claude Code session transcripts (~/.claude/projects/**.jsonl, incl. subagent folders to exclude), Cursor (IDE state.vscdb SQLite under ~/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User plus agent transcripts under ~/.cursor), and OpenAI Codex CLI rollouts (~/.codex/sessions/**). Grok Bot (desktop AI assistant app) conversations are a required LATER source with its own adapter.

Requirements:
- Extract ONLY human-authored messages with timestamps from each source; injected content (tool results, system reminders, task notifications, interrupted-request markers, agent hand-backs) is excluded.
- Shared normalized record (source, session id, project, timestamp, author role, text) emitted by all adapters.
- Counting rules for thanks and F-bomb tokens: word lists in a YAML config, word boundaries, case-insensitive, quoted/pasted text and code blocks excluded; deterministic, no AI in the loop.
- Time period is parameterizable: rolling windows (last 24h, N hours, N days) AND calendar windows (today, yesterday) with a configurable day-start time defaulting to local midnight (e.g. 4am means today runs 4am to 4am), with correct timezone and DST handling.
- Deduplication across forked/resumed sessions, mirrored records, and repeated hand-backs; incremental re-scan without re-reading unchanged files.
- Privacy: local only, no network I/O, no message text in output or scan state; fixtures are synthetic.
- Meter output: counts, ratio gauge, bands; CLI with --window/--day-start/--timezone/--sources/--json flags.

Format claims must cite public docs or source code; unverifiable claims are assumptions verified against a real Mac. Milestones are delivered as the epics under this initiative, in order.

comments.text: Filed by cloud-agent (cursor / glm-5.3) as the step-by-step plan for this initiative. Structure: this initiative holds 9 epics in delivery order — A Foundations (KDATAP-7299f8), B Counting rules (KDATAP-ff3968), C Time windows (KDATAP-5219e2), D Claude Code adapter (KDATAP-5d5c3f), E Cursor adapter (KDATAP-3f3158), F Codex adapter (KDATAP-5ee1c5), G Meter and CLI (KDATAP-07c368), H Privacy/gold eval/release (KDATAP-d59959), and I Grok Bot later-source adapter (KDATAP-247294) — with 39 tasks carrying descriptions, done-when criteria, and blocked-by dependencies. Format claims in descriptions cite public docs or source (Claude Code session docs, openai/codex rollout source, Cursor reverse-engineering references); unverifiable claims are called out as assumptions with verify-on-a-real-Mac tasks (D1, E4, F2, I1). Earlier draft plan doc PR #96 was closed and its branch deleted by request; this Kanbus filing is the record of the plan now.
